rulings.challenge_claim: The 5:1-5:7 bounds are byte-supported at both seams, but the row's original-language engagement misnames the song form it cites, leaves a first-in-the-book universal without a digit, and rests the closing verdict on the rendering while the verse's decisive Hebrew sound-play stays unquoted.
rulings.grounds: Three items, one real, one dead, one over-framed. Seams re-derived and clean: the row's onset splice stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.5.1 and the rear seam holds on the verse-initial woe particle at oshb:Isa.5.8 (both byte tier); span mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (PE at MT 4:6 at the front seam, SAMEKH at MT 5:7 in span; tier-3, single-witness). ITEM (i) UPHELD IN SUBSTANCE BUT ITS DIGITS CARRY THE WRONG COUNT-OBJECT: the four-letter unpointed song form the row cites in device_notes is indeed skeleton grade, unlabeled, and not independently attested at that verse -- as a consonantal string it stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, MT 5:1) and there only INSIDE the cohortative אָשִׁ֤ירָה (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier), the attested free forms being that cohortative and the construct שִׁירַ֥ת (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier). The challenge's digit of 9 verses, and its homograph guard naming the ornament noun at oshb:Isa.3.19, belong to the SHORTER three-letter song skeleton (sweep: 9 verses) -- a different object; MT 3:19 does not carry the four-letter string at all. ITEM (ii) DOES NOT SURVIVE: the universals gate returns GREEN over the row with zero flags, the sentence carrying 'the book's first sung-frame onset' being grounded in an adjacent byte-tier citation, and the claim itself re-derives (5:1 is the first of the frame spine's three song openings). ITEM (iii) IS OVER-FRAMED: the row splices pointed Hebrew at oshb:Isa.5.1 and oshb:Isa.5.7 and its WEB quotations pass verbatim checking at inline web: refs, so the closure does not rest on the translation; the narrower true finding is that the verdict's decisive assonance pair וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה (oshb:Isa.5.7, byte tier) is unquoted while the rendering flattens both pairs (“He looked for justice, but behold, oppression, for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress.”, web:Isa.5.7).
rulings.remedy: (a) In device_notes, replace the unpointed four-letter song form with the pointed construct שִׁירַ֥ת spliced from oshb:Isa.5.1, or keep a mention-grade form and label it skeleton tier. (b) If any digit is set beside it, that sentence must name the swept string -- the four-letter skeleton stands in 1 verse book-wide, the three-letter skeleton in 9. (c) In boundary_rationale, add the pointed splice וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה (oshb:Isa.5.7) with its tier named beside the existing WEB closure quote, so the verdict step carries original-language evidence. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: each new Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse; the Hebrew normalize dry-run reports no degraded run; and the song-form sentence names its swept object, which is the test that killed the original -- a digit swept on the shorter skeleton must no longer be attachable to the four-letter form. No boundary change.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both woe seams and every digit are byte-true, but the cohesion that keeps the consequence verses inside the woe is asserted from the rendering: the bytes there carry no speech verb, and the oath particle that actually binds the consequence is neither quoted nor named.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed from bytes. MT 5:9 opens בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם לֹ֞א (oshb:Isa.5.9, byte tier): no speech verb stands in that clause, and the rendering supplies one (“In my ears, Yahweh of Armies says:”, web:Isa.5.9). The row's strongest_rejected_alternative rests the merge on 'one divine-speech consequence clause that runs without a break and crosses no tier-1 seam', giving no Hebrew and no tier for either half, so the load-bearing cohesion step is carried by the English while the elliptical oath run that would carry the same conclusion from the bytes goes unquoted and unnamed. The row's digits verify exactly: the woe-particle census is 22 verses book-wide (sweep: 22 verses) with six verse-initial in this chapter at MT 5:8, 5:11, 5:18, 5:20, 5:21 and 5:22 (byte-checked verse-initial), and both seams stand where claimed. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 5:7 at the front seam, PE at MT 5:10 in span; tier-3, single-witness). Severity stays low as filed: the defect is engagement, not boundary -- no tier-1 onset intervenes between MT 5:8 and MT 5:11, so the merge itself is not in doubt.
rulings.remedy: In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace 'one divine-speech consequence clause' with a byte-grounded formulation built on the splice בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם לֹ֞א (oshb:Isa.5.9, byte tier): state that the elliptical oath run binds the consequence to the indictment and that the divine speech verb is supplied by the rendering rather than present in the bytes; keep the sentence inside the one-sentence-plus-disclosure limit. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS -- the test that killed the original: the form the sentence relies on must be present in the cited verse's own bytes, so a search of MT 5:9 for a speech verb returns none and the warrant has to rest on the quoted oath run; the splice re-collates at byte tier and the Hebrew normalize dry-run stays clean. No boundary change.

rulings.challenge_claim: The bounds are byte-supported at both woe seams and the title-family distinction the row draws is correct, but that distinction is made in transliteration with no pointed form and misdescribes the attested epithet, while the row's real byte-level cohesion evidence goes unquoted.
rulings.grounds: The engagement half is UPHELD: the row draws a boundary-relevant original-language distinction ('a bare ha-El ha-qadosh epithet') entirely in transliteration, with no pointed splice and no tier named, against the standing requirement that original-language claims be quoted. The bytes read וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.5.16, byte tier). The 'misdescribes the attested epithet' half is REFUTED on those same bytes: the row's own transliteration carries both articles explicitly, so it asserts no articular absence; 'bare' is used in contrast to the construct title -- precisely the distinction the challenge itself concedes is byte-correct and the right hazard call -- and the only element the transliteration leaves unrepresented is the clause conjunction, which is not part of the epithet. The second half is NOT A DEFECT in what the row asserts: the row's stated ground is that no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the reversal couplet from its consequence, and that is byte-true -- the verse-initial tokens from MT 5:12 through MT 5:17 carry no woe particle, no divine-speech frame and no oracle header. The consequence particles לָכֵ֛ן (oshb:Isa.5.13, byte tier) and לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.5.14, byte tier) would strengthen the row, and the challenge's digits for them re-derive exactly (sweep: 3 verses carrying that particle in this chapter, 25 book-wide), but unused stronger evidence is not a defect in the evidence used. Marks verify: no mark falls inside MT 5:11-5:17 and the preceding PE at MT 5:10 is disclosed at the correct type (tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: In device_notes, replace the transliterated epithet with the pointed splice וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ from oshb:Isa.5.16 with its tier named, retaining the existing statement that it is a different count-object from the construct-title census. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: the splice re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse and the Hebrew normalize dry-run reports no degraded run; the repaired sentence must still name which census the epithet is excluded from, which is the discipline the transliteration-only original left unmet. No boundary change, and no obligation to add the consequence particles.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: 'Two byte-false claims about the Holy-One-of-Israel title -- a plene-only undercount and a first-appearance claim that is four chapters late -- plus an undisclosed accent-tier catchword straddling this row's rear seam.' LF: the row's 'first appearance' claim is false and its 24-verse digit undercounts the construct-title census by one, with 1:4 named as 'the omitted earlier site'.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: both lenses hit the same row on the same two claims, but they are TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS, not one -- LF treats them as a single error with a single cause and gets the cause byte-wrong. Re-derived from bytes: the PLENE construct title stands in 24 verses (sweep: 24 verses) and that set ALREADY CONTAINS oshb:Isa.1.4, oshb:Isa.5.19 and oshb:Isa.5.24; the twenty-fifth site is the DEFECTIVE spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier), which the plene string does not reach (sweep: 1 verse), giving 25 title verses, 12 in chs 1-39 and 13 in chs 40-66. So OL's diagnosis is byte-exact and LF's is byte-false: 1:4 is not the omitted site, and a cure that adds 1:4 to a plene-only sweep would still leave the digit wrong. The suffixed epithet קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ in that same verse is a different object and is not counted with the title. DEFECT TWO is independent of the digit: קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.1.4, byte tier) carries the identical construct four chapters earlier, so 'here its first appearance' is false whatever the census total; that verse's rejection verb also recurs at skeleton tier in this chapter's consequence at oshb:Isa.5.24. DEFECT THREE (OL only) is real but small: הָאֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.5.19, byte tier) and הָאֹמְרִ֥ים (oshb:Isa.5.20, byte tier) are identical at accent-stripped tier and differ only in accent at byte tier (sweep: 1 verse at byte tier, 3 at accent-stripped, 4 at skeleton), an undisclosed catchword across the row's rear seam that the rendering hides (“who say,” at web:Isa.5.19 against “Woe to those who call evil good” at web:Isa.5.20) -- but the seam it straddles is held by a verse-initial woe particle at MT 5:20, so it is a disclosure gap, not a boundary defect. SEVERITY settles at medium, not LF's high: both seams, the unit_type and the mark disclosure (SAMEKH at MT 5:19, in span, correctly typed, tier-3 single-witness) are untouched, as LF's own evidence concedes.
rulings.remedy: (a) In boundary_rationale, correct the census to 25 verses AND name the swept object in the same sentence -- 24 plene verses plus the one defective site -- rather than repairing the digit alone. (b) In boundary_rationale, delete 'here its first appearance' and replace it with the byte-true ordinal: this chapter carries the second and third title sites, the first standing at oshb:Isa.1.4. (c) In device_notes, disclose the accent-stripped recurrence of the participle across the rear seam with its tier named; this is a SEAM-PAIR with the following row and is ONE edit covering both sides. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: the digit's sentence must name the swept spelling, so the plene-only needle that produced 24 cannot reproduce it; the corrected ordinal must survive a re-sweep that returns oshb:Isa.1.4 ahead of this chapter -- the test that killed the original; every new Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean Hebrew normalize dry-run. No respan is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The single-verse row's self-contained-content ground is contested by the bytes: its opening participle repeats the preceding verse's closing word at accent tier, and the woe carries no announcement of judgment of its own, the governing consequence particles standing outside the row.
rulings.grounds: ITEM (i) IS BYTE-TRUE IN SUBSTANCE AND BYTE-FALSE IN POSITION. The recurrence is real and undisclosed in both rows: הָאֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.5.19, byte tier) and הָאֹמְרִ֥ים (oshb:Isa.5.20, byte tier) are identical at accent-stripped tier (sweep: 3 verses at that tier) and differ only in accent at byte tier. But the participle OPENS MT 5:19 -- it is that verse's first token -- so 'closes the preceding verse' misplaces the count-object's position; the object is right, the position claim is not. This is the same seam as the preceding row's rear edge: ONE edit, not two. ITEM (ii) OVER-READS: the row's 'self-contained content' claims self-contained INDICTMENT content, which is byte-true of MT 5:20's three inversion pairs, and cutting at each verse-initial woe particle is the sanctioned unit for this series, so the boundary is not contested by the bytes. What IS missing is a disclosure: לָכֵן֩ (oshb:Isa.5.24, byte tier) and עַל כֵּ֡ן (oshb:Isa.5.25, byte tier) stand after four verse-initial woe clauses at MT 5:18, 5:20, 5:21 and 5:22 (all byte-checked verse-initial), none of which carries a consequence of its own, so the stack-plus-shared-consequence reading is a live rival the row never names while its rejected_alternative engages only a whole-series merge. Marks verify (SAMEKH at MT 5:20 in span, SAMEKH at MT 5:19 preceding, both correctly typed, tier-3 single-witness). SEVERITY drops to low: no boundary is displaced and no digit is wrong.
rulings.remedy: (a) Carry the seam-pair disclosure named in the preceding row's remedy -- one edit, stated once, tier named (accent-stripped identity, byte-tier accent difference). (b) In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the whole-series-merge rival with the stronger rival the particles raise: the indictment clauses running from MT 5:18 through MT 5:23 answered by one consequence at MT 5:24-5:25, disclosed and rejected on byte grounds rather than left unnamed; keep it inside the one-sentence-plus-disclosure limit. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: the replacement rival must be the strongest one the chapter's own bytes support -- verified by re-reading the verse-initial tokens from MT 5:18 to MT 5:25, which show no consequence clause inside MT 5:20 -- and any Hebrew added re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run. DISCLOSURE ONLY: no respan is proposed here.

rulings.challenge_claim: Onset, seams and marks are byte-clean, but the row never discloses that the verse it isolates carries no announcement of judgment at all and that the governing consequence particle stands two verses beyond its rear seam.
rulings.grounds: Verified as stated, and correctly held at the disclosure level. MT 5:21 is a two-colon address with no finite judgment clause in its bytes; its woe particle is verse-initial; the following verse-initial woe particle at MT 5:22 holds the rear seam; no parashah mark falls inside the one-verse span and the preceding SAMEKH at MT 5:20 is disclosed at the correct type (tier-3, single-witness). The finite judgment language first enters under לָכֵן֩ (oshb:Isa.5.24, byte tier) and עַל כֵּ֡ן (oshb:Isa.5.25, byte tier), outside the row, so the indictment-to-consequence construction does straddle the rear seam while the row's rejected_alternative weighs only a forward merge with the next woe. The challenge does not assert that the cut is wrong, and the cut is not wrong: hoy-onset units are the operative unit for this series and the absence of a judgment announcement is not a defect against that category -- which is exactly why the finding stands at the disclosure level and at low severity as filed. Form-class labels are held here as the challenge holds them, no morphology layer being staged.
rulings.remedy: In strongest_rejected_alternative, add the stack-plus-shared-consequence rival by verse anchor -- the indictment clauses from MT 5:18 through MT 5:23 answered by one consequence at MT 5:24-5:25 -- alongside the existing forward-merge rival, within the sanctioned one-sentence-plus-disclosure limit. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: the disclosed rival must be the strongest one the chapter's own bytes support, verified by re-reading the verse-initial tokens from MT 5:18 to MT 5:25; no new digit may be written without naming its swept object. AUTHOR-WAVE NOTE: this is the same remedy class as the preceding row and the next one, so it must ship as one consistent disclosure across the three rows under the variation order, not as three ad-hoc formulations. Disclosure only; no boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: 'the title digit repeats the plene-only undercount and the row takes as the sixth woe's own the consequence that the bytes attach to the whole four-fold indictment stack.' LF: the device_notes sweep digit for the title census (24 verses book-wide) 'undercounts the byte-swept total by one', again naming 1:4 as the omitted site.
rulings.grounds: Same convergence and the SAME SPLIT as the earlier title row in this cluster. The digit defect is CONFIRMED: the plene construct string returns 24 verses (sweep: 24 verses) and already contains oshb:Isa.1.4 and this row's own oshb:Isa.5.24; the twenty-fifth is the defective קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier), so the census is 25 (sweep: 24 plene verses + 1 defective verse). OL's diagnosis is byte-exact; LF's naming of 1:4 as the omitted site is byte-false a SECOND time and would yield a cure that still leaves the digit wrong. OL's second item is real and DISTINCT from the first: לָכֵן֩ (oshb:Isa.5.24, byte tier) follows four verse-initial woe clauses at MT 5:18, 5:20, 5:21 and 5:22, none carrying a consequence of its own, so reading MT 5:24-5:25 as the sixth woe's alone is one construal of two and the bytes do not settle it; the row discloses the refrain-bridge rival but not this one. Everything else re-derives exactly: the closing refrain בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.5.25, byte tier), re-swept from its own source bytes, returns byte tier at exactly five verses -- oshb:Isa.5.25, oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, oshb:Isa.9.16 = web:Isa.9.17, oshb:Isa.9.20 = web:Isa.9.21 and oshb:Isa.10.4 = web:Isa.10.4 (sweep: 5 verses at byte tier) -- so 'byte-identical' is honest and all three offset-zone duals are arithmetically and content-correct; the in-span SAMEKH at MT 5:23 is disclosed at the correct type (tier-3, single-witness). NEW FINDING, raised by neither lens on this cluster: the row's strongest_rejected_alternative settles the close by naming a governance granularity rule in row prose -- 'the HYBRID rule that refrains close units' -- instead of arguing the bracket function from the bytes, which is the register class one lens flags on a row in this assignment's other cluster and which the governing rule itself directs be argued from bytes.
rulings.remedy: (a) In device_notes, correct the census to 25 verses and name the swept object in the same sentence (24 plene verses plus the one defective site). (b) In device_notes, add the stack-plus-shared-consequence construal as a disclosed rival beside the existing refrain-bridge rival, verse-anchored to MT 5:18-5:23 and MT 5:24-5:25. (c) In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the named governance rule with the byte argument for the refrain's bracket function -- its five byte-tier sites and its position at this stanza's end -- keeping the rival disclosure intact. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: the digit's sentence must name the swept spelling so a plene-only needle cannot return 24 again (the test that killed the original); the rewritten rejected_alternative must contain no governance-rule name and must stay within the one-sentence-plus-disclosure limit; every Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run; every offset-zone ref keeps its dual. No respan is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rear seam is argued from a chapter end plus the absence of an intervening onset while the tier-1 evidence one verse later is neither quoted nor cited, and a five-verse continuity claim runs unquoted through a doubled-token verse whose form the row declines to name.
rulings.grounds: ITEM (i) UPHELD and it is the substantive finding. The row's rear-seam sentence disclaims the chapter division as non-cutting and then closes 'with the chapter' on the absence of a further onset -- an absence argument resting on tier-4 metadata -- while positive tier-1 evidence stands one verse later in בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier), a dated frame followed immediately by a first-person vision verb, rendered “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up;” (web:Isa.6.1); that verse is neither quoted nor carried in boundary_evidence_refs, so the strongest available byte ground for the seam the row wants is simply absent from the row. The supporting lens's contrary reading -- that no chapter-boundary argument drives the rear seam -- is not borne out by the row's own sentence. ITEM (ii) REFUTED on the bytes and on the rule: the staged extract does carry the doubled pair ושאג יִשְׁאַ֨ג (oshb:Isa.5.29; first member unpointed as staged, second at byte tier), but the row discloses the ketiv/qere note as single-witness and expressly leaves its content unsliced, which is exactly what the standing rule requires -- check the inventory before counting or slicing -- and the row neither counts nor slices there; the mark and K/Q gate returns GREEN over the row. No standing rule obliges a row to name which member it reads where nothing is counted or sliced, so this charge is register-level strictness, not a defect. ITEM (iii) UPHELD AT LOW: the row's only pointed splice is its opening run at oshb:Isa.5.26, so the boundary-relevant claim that MT 5:26-5:30 runs as one uninterrupted sentence-chain -- a Hebrew-syntactic claim -- is carried by the rendering alone. NEW FINDING, raised by neither lens: the row's strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes both settle the seam by naming a governance granularity rule in row prose ('the HYBRID rule that refrains close units') rather than arguing bracket function from the bytes, the same register class carried over from the preceding row. Marks verify (PE at MT 5:30 in span, correctly typed, tier-3 single-witness) and the row's offset-zone duals are arithmetically right.
rulings.remedy: (a) In boundary_rationale, replace the chapter-end-plus-absence rear-seam ground with positive tier-1 evidence: splice בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה from oshb:Isa.6.1 with its tier named, argue the seam from the dated frame and the first-person vision onset, and add that verse to boundary_evidence_refs. (b) In boundary_rationale, ground the five-verse continuity claim with at least one pointed splice from inside MT 5:27-5:30 with its tier named, or restate the claim at the tier the evidence actually supports. (c) In strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes, replace the named governance rule with the byte argument for the refrain's bracket function. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS -- the test that killed the original: the rear seam must stand on a form quoted from a cited verse's own bytes rather than on the absence of one, and the refs-mirror check must find the newly argued verse in boundary_evidence_refs; each added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run; the rewritten fields carry no governance-rule name. The boundary itself is unchanged -- this is an evidence and register repair, not a respan.
